newsitem.title: USA: NYC sees $7 mln loss for 1-wk sales tax exemption.
newsitem.headline: NYC sees $7 mln loss for 1-wk sales tax exemption.

text.p: The New York City Council on Wednesday said that it had approved giving the city's shoppers a one-week moratorium on sales taxes for clothing and shoes, adding that it estimated the step would cost it $7 million.

Council sources, who requested anonymity, had indicated that it likely would take advantage of a provision in the state budget that allows communities to approve bills that mirror the same one-week exemption New York State adopted.

The head of the council's finance committee, Herbert Berman, in prepared remarks, said, "This will provide a well-needed boost for New York City merchants during what is traditionally the slowest retail month of the year."

The council approved the measure by a vote of 34 to 13. But all of the members who represent minority communities turned the proposal down, saying they disagreed with it because it will be the week of January 18. This week includes Martin Luther King's birthday, and they did not want to link the holiday with commerce, a City Hall source said.
Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, who emphasized that the city needed to rebuild the retail sector at a Crain's New York business breakfast, said he planned to ask the council to approve the measure.
A City Council finance official declined to project how much the one-week moratorium will produce in extra spending, saying there were too many variables.

The total exemption from sales taxes adds up to 8.25 cent for New York City residents. Both the city and state will waive their four percent sales taxes and the Metropolitan Transportation Authority will waive its 0.25 percent portion.
